Tuesday 29 September 2026 11:07, UK Image: Mauricio Pochettino was in charge at Spurs between 2014 and 2019 Former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino says the Premier League "lived through a period of deception" if Manchester City breached financial rules. Reports last Friday said an independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115-charge case between the league and the club, and Sky Sports News understands the process is moving to the appeal stage. Pochettino, who was in charge of Spurs from 2014 to 2019 and Chelsea in 2023-24, having previously managed Southampton from 2013 to 2014, said it had warped the view of history. messages.text: 'Ferrari has made its choices' - Vasseur given full backing after Horner speculation

metadata.summary: Ferrari have reiterated their "full confidence" in Frederic Vasseur as team principal after speculation around his future was fuelled by Christian Horner suggesting interest in the role, with the Italian marque making clear it "has made its choices" around who leads the F1 team.
metadata.content: Frederic Vasseur: Ferrari state 'full confidence' in F1 team principal after Christian Horner comments and speculation | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Frederic Vasseur: Ferrari state 'full confidence' in F1 team principal after Christian Horner comments and speculation "Ferrari has made its choices and has full confidence in the leadership of Fred Vasseur and his team and we will continue to do so"; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia live on Sky Sports from Friday morning F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix Tuesday 29 September 2026 11:33, UK Image: Frederic Vasseur is in his fourth season in charge of F1's most famous team Ferrari have reiterated their "full confidence" in Frederic Vasseur as team principal after speculation around his future was fuelled by Christian Horner suggesting interest in the role, with the Italian marque making clear it "has made its choices" around who leads the F1 team. Vasseur admitted after last Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix that the team were "not working in perfect serenity" amid persistent and "frustrating" rumours around his position at the Scuderia. That was amplified last week by an interview with Horner published in The Times in which the former Red Bull team principal said Ferrari were the only outfit he would consider returning to the pit-wall for without the ownership stake that he has been prioritising for any comeback to the sport. messages.text: Antonelli vows to ‘re-establish the order’ over Russell at Bahrain GP

metadata.summary: World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he will "re-establish the order" over George Russell at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix after being outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate in Azerbaijan.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli vows to 're-establish the order' over George Russell at Bahrain GP in Malaysia after losing out in Azerbaijan | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Kimi Antonelli vows to 're-establish the order' over George Russell at Bahrain GP in Malaysia after losing out in Azerbaijan George Russell won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix to reduce his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead to 66 points with eight rounds remaining; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia live on Sky Sports from Friday morning F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix Monday 28 September 2026 16:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli says that the Azerbaijan GP was 'one of those days you have to be happy with P5' but adds that he will be 'back at my level' at the Malaysian Grand Prix. World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he will "re-establish the order" over George Russell at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix after being outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate in Azerbaijan. Antonelli had finished ahead of Russell in five successive Grands Prix but could only manage fifth in Baku, as the Brit produced his best weekend of the season to claim victory from pole position. The result cut Antonelli's lead over his Mercedes team-mate to 66 points with eight rounds remaining. metadata.summary: England manager Sarina Wiegman has named a 23-player squad for next month’s World Cup qualifying play-off against Greece, with Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly both missing out.
metadata.content: England Women: Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly miss out as Sarina Wiegman names squad to face Greece in World Cup qualifiers | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England Women: Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly miss out as Sarina Wiegman names squad to face Greece in World Cup qualifiers England manager Sarina Wiegman has named a 23-player squad for next month’s World Cup qualifying play-off against Greece; Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly not included; captain Leah Williamson returns after missing June's fixtures with injury Tuesday 29 September 2026 11:44, UK Image: Chloe Kelly (left) and Ella Toone have not been included in England's 23-player squad to face Greece England manager Sarina Wiegman has named a 23-player squad for next month’s World Cup qualifying play-off against Greece, with Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly both missing out. As well as the Manchester United midfielder and Arsenal forward being left out, Chelsea forward Aggie Beever-Jones and the Arsenal duo Lotte Wubben-Moy and Taylor Hinds have also been omitted from the squad. However, captain Leah Williamson does return after missing June's 4-0 defeat by Spain and the 3-0 victory over Ukraine with injury. Meanwhile, Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter earns her first call-up to the senior squad and there is also return for both Liverpool defender Grace Fisk and the uncapped North Carolina Courage midfielder Erica Meg Parkinson after her debut in April. messages.text: Whyte wants Fisher after injury hell - 'I fought Itauma with a broken foot!'

metadata.summary: Dillian Whyte provided a gruesome description while explaining the agonising injury that he suffered, just weeks before his last fight against Moses Itauma.
metadata.content: Dillian Whyte was suffering from a broken foot in Moses Itauma defeat but wants to return in British battle with Johnny Fisher | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Dillian Whyte was suffering from a broken foot in Moses Itauma defeat but wants to return in British battle with Johnny Fisher Dillian Whyte has revealed that he was suffering from a broken foot in his defeat by Moses Itauma last August; Whyte fractured his foot during his training camp and then injured it again in the changing room; 'The Body Snatcher' wants to return against Johnny Fisher this year Tuesday 29 September 2026 06:16, UK Image: Dillian Whyte wants to return to the ring before the end of the year Dillian Whyte provided a gruesome description while explaining the agonising injury that he suffered, just weeks before his last fight against Moses Itauma. "It felt like someone had dropped a dumbbell on my foot," revealed Whyte when asked to put into words the pain caused by the fractured foot that he sustained in training last summer. "I was running and I felt it [my foot] and then I went to spar and I was sparring big, agile guys and someone was pressing me, I stepped back the wrong way and then it just fractured clean. "It was terrible, but we're used to pulling off miracles. We're used to fighting injured. "I made the best of the situation and had a decent camp. I felt good during fight week and really thought I would beat Moses." Dillian Whyte 'well up' for fight with Johnny Fisher

messages.text: Littler in shock first-round exit at World Grand Prix as Van Gerwen also beaten

metadata.summary: Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix as he lost out 2-1 to Luke Woodhouse in Leicester, on the same night that six-time winner Michael van Gerwen was also eliminated.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Littler in shock first-round exit as defending champion loses to Luke Woodhouse | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Littler in shock first-round exit as defending champion loses to Luke Woodhouse World No 1 Luke Littler suffers shock 2-1 defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night in Leicester as six-time champion Michael van Gerwen is also eliminated; watch day two of the World Grand Prix live on Sky Sports+ from 6pm, Tuesday Tuesday 29 September 2026 11:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the World Grand Prix match between Luke Littler and Luke Woodhouse Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix as he lost out 2-1 to Luke Woodhouse in Leicester, on the same night that six-time winner Michael van Gerwen was also eliminated. Littler won the first set, but was far from his best as Woodhouse spurned several chances at double to have taken the opener into a deciding leg. Woodhouse made no mistake in sets two and three, however, to see him pull off one of the biggest upsets in the hostory of the double-in, double-out tournament.
